title: Clearance-Constrained PCB Global Placement with Heterogeneous Components
problem: PCB placement must handle pad-to-pad clearance constraints and heterogeneous components while minimizing routing congestion and overlap.
motivation: Advanced PCB design complexity and time-to-market pressures make automated placement tools essential; existing academic placers overlook practical constraints like clearance rules and heterogeneous component handling.
method: The framework combines four complementary models. First, a wire-area model predicts how much routing space power and signal connections will consume, accounting for congestion. Second, a pad-to-pad clearance model enforces minimum distances between connection points to prevent interference. Third, a two-sided density model prevents component bodies from overlapping with each other and prevents pads (connection points) from overlapping. Fourth, a quadratic programming-based legalizer (a mathematical optimizer) adjusts component positions to resolve any remaining clearance violations and overlaps.
key_novelty: This is the first PCB placement framework that directly enforces clearance between pads and handles components of different sizes and shapes simultaneously.
contributions: Wire-area model for routing resource estimation
QP-based legalizer for mixed-shape component legalization
limitations: Specific benchmark circuits and industrial design rules not detailed; comparison with commercial PCB tools not provided.
primary_theme: Constraint-aware PCB placement with heterogeneous components
